title: High Salt Nuclear Extract Preparation
author: Xavier Contreras
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kh2ct8e

steps.title: Pellet cells and wash
steps.instruction: Keep tubes on ice; centrifuge cells at 1500 × g for 8 min in an appropriate tube (e.g., 50 mL); discard supernatant; wash cells once with PBS; centrifuge at 1000 × g for 10 min; discard all supernatant and record the packed cell volume (PCV) for each tube.

steps.title: Resuspend and swell cells
steps.instruction: Fill each tube with hypotonic buffer (HB) and gently resuspend the cells; centrifuge at 1000 × g for 5 min; verify that the swollen cell volume (SCV) is greater than the PCV; carefully pour off supernatant (pellet may be loose); add 2 × PCV volume of HB, resuspend gently; place on ice for 10 min.

steps.title: Dounce cells and isolate nuclei
steps.instruction: Dounce the swollen cells 15 times (HeLa S3; adjust for other cell types); check for lysis by microscopy; spin the homogenate at 2600 × g for 15 min; record the nuclear pellet volume (NPV); remove and discard the cytoplasmic supernatant.

steps.title: Prepare salt extracts
steps.instruction: Calculate NPV/2; split this volume into two tubes—one for low‑salt buffer, one for high‑salt buffer; to each add β‑mercaptoethanol at 0.0007 × NPV/2 and PMSF (0.2 M) at 0.01 × NPV/2; mix well; resuspend nuclear pellets in ½ low‑salt buffer and dounce 6 times; while mixing continuously add the high‑salt buffer; continue mixing for 30 min after the addition is complete.

steps.title: Spin and store extract
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixture at 15 000 × g for 30 min; recover the supernatant (high‑salt nuclear extract); snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.
